not_served.reason: reachable, but the dataflow is 'Oil products stock levels - monthly data': stock LEVELS, not days of cover. Deriving days would need a consumption series and would be MODELLED, so no row is shipped

no fetched open source publishes a days-of-cover figure for them; Eurostat nrg_stk_oilm gives stock LEVELS only (see not_served entry above), IEA oil stocks was not served. A days figure would need a consumption series and would be MODELLED, so none is shipped.

policy.adds_only: Reference figures per commodity class and geography. Edits no graph.json field.
policy.labels: Every row is SOURCED (the published number, with a unit conversion shown where used). The graph's own inventory_days defaults are MODELLED and are only described in `engine_assumptions`, not as rows.
policy.opt_in: Read only when a caller asks (GET /graph/inventory-days, or the loader). No engine, sim or portsim code reads this file; every id and byte of every run is unchanged without it.
policy.ratio_vs_days: EIA publishes days of supply. Census publishes inventory-to-sales (or to-shipments) ratios in months; `days_equivalent` is the ratio times 30.4375 and is a unit conversion, not a separate measurement.
policy.scope: Each row applies only to the class and geography in its `scope` field (here: United States). Nothing is extrapolated to another country, port or class.
